description: Test the functionality of pagination controls to navigate through multiple pages of listed connectors.
steps: Navigate to the Connectors page using the 'Connectors' tab.
Verify the visibility of pagination controls, including buttons for 'First', '«', '»', 'Last', and numbered pages.
Click on the button for page '2' and verify that the connectors list updates to display page 2 results.
Click on the '»' button and verify that the next page of connectors is displayed.
Click on the 'Last' button and verify that the last page of connectors is displayed.
Click on the 'First' button and verify that the first page of connectors is displayed.
Click on the '«' button to navigate back to the previous page and verify results.
expected_results: Each pagination button navigates to the correct page.
Connector list updates correctly based on page selection.
No duplicate or missing connectors are displayed.
edge_cases: Navigating to a non-existent page returns an error gracefully.
Rapid clicking on pagination buttons does not break the UI.
Empty pages are handled without crashing.
Pagination buttons are disabled for out-of-bound pages.
Last page button works correctly for varying numbers of pages.
data_requirements: A list of connectors spanning multiple pages.
Valid user session with access to pagination controls.
Database connection for fetching paginated data.
dependencies: System must contain multiple pages of connectors.
api_interactions: GET request to fetch connectors for specific pages.
performance_metrics: Memory usage while rendering paginated data.
accessibility_requirements: Pagination buttons must be operable using keyboard controls.
Buttons must have descriptive ARIA labels.
Focus state should be visible for all buttons.
Paginated content must be navigable using screen readers.
Contrast ratio for pagination controls must meet WCAG standards.
